reports.primary_endpoint: Survival and rate of functional decline
reports.finding: Survival favored riluzole.
reports.safety: Asthenia, spasticity and aminotransferase elevations were reported.

reports.finding: Decline was smaller in the selected early-stage cohort.
reports.safety: Treatment-emergent events occurred in 84% of each arm.
reports.other_findings: The selected population limits generalization.

reports.primary_endpoint: Week-28 ALSFRS-R change in the prespecified faster-progressing SOD1 subgroup
reports.finding: No significant clinical benefit at 28 weeks. Biomarkers fell.
reports.safety: Neurologic serious adverse events occurred in 7% of recipients.
reports.other_findings: CSF SOD1 and plasma neurofilament declined. Delayed-start follow-up has a different comparison.

reports.population: Early ALS, 239 in the modified intention-to-treat analysis
reports.route: Oral arimoclomol citrate, 400 mg three times daily
reports.primary_endpoint: Combined Assessment of Function and Survival at 76 weeks
reports.finding: No improvement in the primary function/survival endpoint.
reports.safety: Treatment-related events were more common. Adverse events led to discontinuation in 16% versus 5%.
reports.other_findings: Clinical target engagement was insufficiently characterized. A higher systemic dose raised tolerability concerns.

reports.finding: Survival was 65% versus 54%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.41–1.33. Progression also showed no significant benefit.
reports.safety: Comparative adverse-event details were unavailable in the abstract.
reports.other_findings: Limb-onset subgroup HR 0.50, CI 0.24–1.04; the bulbar subgroup estimate pointed the other way. Neither establishes subgroup efficacy.

reports.primary_endpoint: Death, persistent assisted ventilation or tracheostomy
reports.finding: No survival or functional benefit.
reports.safety: No important adverse reactions reported.

reports.design: Randomized placebo-controlled HEALEY phase II/III regimen
reports.primary_endpoint: Joint rate of ALSFRS-R progression and survival over 24 weeks
reports.finding: No evidence of slower disease progression.
reports.safety: Serious adverse events were more frequent in the active arm. Investigators attributed none of seven active-arm deaths to trehalose.
reports.other_findings: No supportive secondary biomarker or clinical effect.

reports.route: Oral memantine up to 20 mg twice daily
reports.finding: No significant difference in progression.
reports.safety: 52 completed treatment. Attrition limits interpretation; the abstract does not attribute all discontinuations to toxicity.
reports.other_findings: Neurofilament and neuropsychiatric outcomes supplied no efficacy signal.

reports.design: Double-blind randomized MND-SMART platform, stage-two analysis
reports.route: Separate oral memantine, trazodone and shared placebo arms
reports.primary_endpoint: ALSFRS-R slope at interim assessment; survival also assessed
reports.finding: Neither arm slowed functional decline or improved survival.
reports.safety: Serious adverse events occurred in 20% on memantine, 14% on trazodone and 13% on placebo.
reports.other_findings: The two active ingredients were evaluated separately.

reports.finding: No phase III efficacy and a material excess of serious hepatobiliary events at the tested regimen.
reports.safety: Serious hepatobiliary events in 41 treated participants (12%) versus none on placebo.
reports.other_findings: Earlier stages suggested a slower ALSFRS-R decline. The confirmatory stage did not reproduce it.

reports.route: Oral minocycline titrated to 400 mg/day for nine months
reports.finding: Function declined faster on minocycline: 1.30 versus 1.04 ALSFRS-R points/month, p=0.005.
reports.safety: Gastrointestinal and neurologic adverse events were also more common.
reports.other_findings: Mortality and FVC differences were not statistically significant. Preclinical neuroprotection did not predict the human result.

reports.primary_endpoint: Rate of decline of maximal voluntary isometric arm strength
reports.finding: No measured functional or survival benefit.
reports.safety: Tolerated at the studied dose without increased overall adverse events.
reports.other_findings: CSF PGE2 was not elevated at baseline and did not fall on treatment.

reports.population: People with ALS and symptomatic cramps
reports.finding: Controlled evidence supports fewer symptomatic cramps.
reports.safety: Reported as generally well tolerated at this dose.
reports.other_findings: The clinical question was cramp relief. Alex's chart does not record cramps.

reports.finding: No strength, survival or functional benefit.
reports.safety: Combined phase II/III analyses showed faster FVC decline in the gabapentin group.
reports.other_findings: The pooled respiratory finding is separate from the phase III primary endpoint.

reports.primary_endpoint: Rate of loss of maximal isometric arm strength
reports.finding: Arm strength declined faster on topiramate (p=0.012).
reports.safety: Weight loss, anorexia and other adverse events were more frequent. Both weakness and weight loss are relevant to Alex.

reports.finding: No significant difference in primary survival outcome.
reports.safety: Adverse-event frequencies were comparable; respiratory failure occurred in both arms.
reports.other_findings: A post hoc faster-progressor signal requires prospective confirmation.

reports.route: Oral pioglitazone 45 mg/day added to riluzole
reports.finding: Stopped for futility. No survival improvement.
reports.safety: Described as well tolerated. The trial stopped for futility.

reports.design: Uncontrolled human safety study with separate cell and mouse experiments
reports.primary_endpoint: Safety and circulating oxidative damage; no controlled clinical efficacy endpoint
reports.finding: A serum oxidative-stress marker fell. Human functional or survival benefit remains unresolved.
reports.safety: The authors reported tolerability during follow-up.
reports.other_findings: Survival extension was observed in SOD1 mice. The human measurement was serum protein carbonyls.

reports.design: Unblinded within-person pilot with a three-month baseline
reports.population: 20 with motor neuron disease including ALS
reports.primary_endpoint: Changes in cramp severity/frequency and spasticity
reports.finding: Cramp and phasic spasticity measures improved without a concurrent placebo group.
reports.safety: The authors reported good tolerability.
reports.other_findings: A blinded symptomatic trial would clarify the signal.

reports.primary_endpoint: Joint function and survival rank at 12 months
reports.finding: No prespecified clinical efficacy endpoint improved. Neutropenia occurred in 8% versus 2% (37 versus 8 people).
reports.safety: The comparative hematologic toxicity is the harm basis; the study described overall tolerability as generally good.

reports.route: Oral minocycline 100 mg/day plus riluzole versus riluzole alone
reports.primary_endpoint: Combination safety; serial function and respiratory assessment
reports.finding: No significant adverse effects were detected in this pilot.
reports.safety: Twenty patients and six months of follow-up give limited power for safety.
reports.other_findings: The subsequent larger phase III minocycline trial documented functional harm.

reports.population: 84 people with ALS; 44 in the PK subset
reports.route: Oral 25, 50 or 100 mg three times daily
reports.finding: CSF concentrations rose with oral dose; exposure in the target motor neurons was not established.
reports.safety: Up to 300 mg/day was tolerated in this short study.

reports.population: 38 with rapidly progressive SOD1 ALS randomized
reports.route: Oral arimoclomol 200 mg three times daily
reports.finding: The pilot did not establish efficacy. Secondary survival estimate HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.32–1.80).
reports.safety: Tolerability was acceptable in this small cohort.
reports.other_findings: The secondary functional and survival estimates favored treatment imprecisely. Alex has no documented SOD1 result.

reports.finding: Open-label extension supplies longer-term safety observations without a concurrent efficacy control.
reports.safety: 21 of 120 had serious adverse events. Attribution cannot be inferred from the count.

reports.design: Early human ALS intervention report; abstract unavailable
reports.population: ALS participants; details unavailable in indexed record
reports.route: N-acetylcysteine; route not verified in primary index
reports.primary_endpoint: Primary endpoint unavailable in accessible record
reports.finding: A citation was found but no usable primary clinical outcome could be abstracted.
reports.safety: Safety details unavailable.

reports.population: ALS; recruiting in the consulted registry
reports.route: Acetylcysteine plus EH301 on background riluzole
reports.finding: Results unavailable in the registry. This registration supplies no independent evidence of administration or efficacy.
reports.safety: No posted safety outcomes.

reports.population: 63 people with probable or definite ALS
reports.finding: No difference in primary or secondary measures.
reports.safety: Adverse events and laboratory changes were comparable to placebo.

reports.population: 20 people with sporadic ALS on riluzole
reports.route: Oral memantine 10 mg twice daily plus riluzole
reports.primary_endpoint: Safety and CSF biomarkers; function tracked descriptively
reports.finding: CSF tau fell in the treated cohort. No placebo-controlled slowing of decline was demonstrated.
reports.safety: Reported as well tolerated.
reports.other_findings: Biomarker-response subgroups were exploratory.

reports.design: Two small blinded placebo-controlled feasibility studies
reports.route: Oral minocycline 200 mg/day or escalating to 400 mg/day
reports.finding: Pilot feasibility did not establish benefit.
reports.safety: Laboratory elevations and a gastrointestinal-event trend occurred at the higher regimen.

reports.population: ALS participants in a phase II selection trial
reports.primary_endpoint: Six-month ALSFRS-R decline used to select a combination
reports.finding: Celecoxib/creatine was selected over minocycline/creatine; effects of individual ingredients could not be isolated.
reports.safety: Rash was more frequent with celecoxib/creatine.
reports.other_findings: A historical comparison did not establish placebo-controlled benefit.

reports.population: ALS patients; indexed primary record has no abstract
reports.finding: Oral tolerability was reported. No usable comparative efficacy estimate was available.
reports.safety: Limited primary safety detail in the indexed report.

reports.population: ALS participants with reported melatonin use and comparison nonusers
reports.route: Self-reported exposure; dosing and route not standardized
reports.finding: An association with longer survival and slower functional decline is vulnerable to confounding and selection bias.
reports.safety: Safety was not the primary question.
reports.other_findings: Exposure was not assigned in this analysis.

reports.design: Open-label DIGAP-stratified pilot with lead-in; no matched placebo group for melatonin
reports.population: 14 assigned to the impaired autophagy/axonal transport stratum
reports.route: Melatonin; formulation not specified in registry intervention description
reports.primary_endpoint: ALSFRS-R from baseline through month nine
reports.finding: Mean ALSFRS-R was 34.4 at month three before treatment (14 measured) and 30.8 at month nine (13 measured). The design cannot establish a causal treatment effect.
reports.safety: One of 14 in the melatonin stratum had a serious adverse event. Causality unknown.
reports.other_findings: This clinical outcome is distinct from serum markers and from the PRO-ACT observational association.

reports.primary_endpoint: Maximal voluntary isometric contraction of eight arm muscles
reports.finding: No measured strength or functional benefit over six months.
reports.safety: Creatine was well tolerated.

reports.primary_endpoint: Quantitative strength; respiratory function and ALSFRS also assessed
reports.finding: Motor, respiratory and functional measures did not significantly improve.
reports.safety: No safety estimate used for advancement.

reports.route: Oral loading followed by maintenance creatine
reports.finding: Short-term strength increases after loading were followed by progressive decline.
reports.safety: Comparative safety was not established.

reports.population: 14 treated advanced ALS patients and 13 controls
reports.finding: Respiratory measures showed no consistent improvement; later dropout limited comparison.
reports.safety: Comparative adverse events were not quantified in the abstract.

reports.finding: Plasma exposure rose with dose. Brain creatine MRS increased 8% (p=0.06).
reports.safety: No safety concerns reported in six participants.
reports.other_findings: Spectroscopy provides human exposure context but no evidence of clinical benefit.

reports.population: ALS participants assigned high-dose creatine or tamoxifen regimens
reports.finding: Higher-dose tamoxifen ranked numerically ahead of creatine. No placebo group to establish efficacy.
reports.safety: Drug-related adverse events and discontinuations were more frequent with high-dose creatine.

reports.population: ALS patients in expanded access, including prior HEALEY participants
reports.primary_endpoint: Safety and biological activity; function tracked
reports.finding: Function declined over follow-up. No concurrent control established efficacy.
reports.safety: Serious adverse events and deaths occurred; investigators reported no unexpected treatment-related risk.

reports.design: Early stages of the later multistage randomized trial
reports.population: ALS participants in stages one and two
reports.primary_endpoint: CSF exposure and tolerability for dose selection
reports.finding: Both doses exceeded the prespecified CSF trough threshold; no independent replicate of stage-three efficacy.
reports.safety: Biliary events were more frequent with ceftriaxone.

reports.design: Human plasma/CSF PK analysis of the same trial
reports.primary_endpoint: CSF concentration relative to an in-vitro-derived threshold
reports.finding: Both regimens maintained CSF levels above the modeled threshold. Human tissue EAAT2 engagement remained uncertain.
reports.safety: No separate controlled safety comparison in this analysis.

reports.finding: Exploratory changes cannot isolate a celecoxib effect.
reports.safety: The combination was generally tolerated in this pilot.

reports.design: Blinded randomized PARADIGM phase IIb with open-label extension
reports.primary_endpoint: Safety and tolerability; prespecified biomarker endpoints
reports.finding: Signals during follow-up favor further study of the combination. The trial did not demonstrate primary clinical efficacy of celecoxib alone.
reports.safety: The authors reported tolerability; Alex's riluzole screen excludes ciprofloxacin.
reports.other_findings: Exploratory clinical outcomes and biomarkers remain combination-specific.

reports.finding: Dose-related decreases in cramps were observed as secondary effects. Progression estimates were imprecise.
reports.safety: The higher dose caused frequent discontinuation.
reports.other_findings: Relief of cramps and change in disease progression are different outcomes.

reports.route: Oral mexiletine with riluzole versus riluzole alone
reports.finding: No functional benefit at 300 mg/day.
reports.safety: Reported adverse-event proportions were 33% and 20%.

reports.finding: Electrophysiology findings do not establish slowed disability.
reports.safety: Four weeks of observation; long-term risks unresolved.

reports.route: Oral gabapentin 800 mg three times daily
reports.finding: A favorable trend did not reach significance; phase III did not confirm benefit.

reports.design: Open-label screening study with historical comparisons

reports.other_findings: Historical cohorts differed in symptom duration.

reports.design: Randomized controlled trial with an augmented historical comparison

reports.design: Secondary analysis of the RAS-ALS trial
reports.population: Patients in the original randomized trial

reports.finding: No significant slowing of progression. CSF changes cannot be assigned to either ingredient alone.

reports.population: 162 in the regimen primary efficacy analysis

exposure.finding: IV dosing bypassed intestinal degradation. The HEALEY and expanded-access reports do not identify an exposure-limited ALS response. A FUS nanoparticle experiment used trehalose in the formulation and measured delivery of another cargo.

delivery_change.finding: No reviewed drug-specific study showed that motor-cortex sonication corrects the relevant exposure or engagement limitation for this clinical outcome. The four-person ALS feasibility study measured temporary gadolinium enhancement.

delivery_change.finding: No reviewed drug-specific study showed that motor-cortex sonication corrects the relevant exposure or engagement limitation for this clinical outcome. The four-person ALS feasibility study measured temporary gadolinium enhancement.

policy.scope: All eligible frozen DRKG compounds may enter discovery. Verified human ALS administration identifies the subset with prior trial evidence. Unknown testing status is preserved.
policy.harm: A controlled human finding of worse clinical function or credible consequential toxicity overrides possible benefit. Record routine tolerability, withdrawals and non-attributed events separately from this exclusion.
policy.conflict: Discordant controlled primary clinical results for the same therapeutic question remain unresolved. Retain the populations and regimens. Secondary, uncontrolled, biomarker, animal and observational findings cannot establish primary clinical benefit.
policy.delivery: For a negative trial require independent, specific evidence of inadequate exposure or engagement at the intended site and evidence that the proposed focused-ultrasound delivery of this ingredient could correct it. Generic permeability or missing measurements alone cannot satisfy either requirement.
policy.order: Favorable clinical evidence, then supported delivery research after a negative trial, then mechanistic discovery with case-matched safety clearance and a sourced graph rationale.

search.method: Europe PMC title/abstract drug and alias searches, controlled and early-phase reports, ClinicalTrials.gov condition/intervention searches, targeted PK, delivery and citation follow-up. Result IDs include irrelevant matches and studies of the same cohort; findings are adjudicated in reports, never counted as votes. Citation-only and observational evidence are labeled. Comparator treatments are presented for context. This bounded English-language/indexed review can miss unpublished and unindexed trials.
